title: System logic
intro: How O2S decides: the stages a record moves through, who gets which job on Today and when, when a job escalates and to whom, the stuck rules, cover and send-back paths, and what happens when 2 people save at once. Each item names the function in o2s.html and the test that pins it; numbers and limits are on the Formulas tab.

items.title: Order line stage on the PO tracker (lineBucket, orderBucket)

blocks.p: A line's stage is worked out from its quantities every time it is drawn. Nothing is stored as a stage. The checks run in this order and the first one that fits wins. 0.5 Kg/L is the rounding allowance used everywhere.

head: Order of check
Test on the line
Stage
rows: close short approved and not reopened
produced > 0, or production started, or raw material ready

states.name: Order line stage
rows: raw material ready, or production starts (Production)
packing reaches ordered, or packed stock waits for QA
Plant Manager or COO approves a close short
a holder of po.reopen reopens the line

blocks.p: The order's stage is the least advanced stage among its lines (orderBucket takes the lowest). So an order reads Closed short only when every line is closed short, and Delivered only when every line is delivered or closed. Owner shown on the tracker per stage: PO Created and RM Check Supply Chain, Production Production, Lab QC Lab Rep, QA Pre-shipment QA Inspector, Shipment Supply Chain (BUCKET_META).

blocks.note: Delivered is decided by quantity, not by a date (24i). Closed short is checked before Delivered on purpose, so a line closed after a part delivery never reads as delivered.

items.title: The older line stage list (lineStage, stageOf)
items.ask: 2 stage lists live side by side (lineBucket on the tracker, lineStage in some production counts). Should they: A stay as they are, B all move to lineBucket, C you want to see where each is used first?

blocks.p: A second stage list is still in the file and is used by a few production counts (prodWorkCounts 'to make', and 3 other places). It reads flags, not quantities.

blocks.note: STAGE_ORDER lists 'RM / Procurement' but lineStage never returns it. 2 stage lists can disagree for the same line (for example a line packed in full reads QA Pre-shipment on the tracker and Produced here).

items.title: Batch stage, open or closed, and reconciled

blocks.p: batchStage gives each batch 1 heading. It is read from the numbers; only status and reconciled are stored.

head: Order of check
Test
Batch stage
rows: status closed, remainder (produced - packed - disposed) > 0.5 and nothing packable

blocks.note: Ready to pack is counted by batchPackNow, not by the heading: a batch still producing that holds a certified lot is in both lists (26 Aug). batchPackNow also needs a lab-approved lot and refuses pools and voided batches.

states.name: Batch status
rows: Production (batch.close) closes it; a short yield needs a variance reason; Plant Manager gets Yield short
Production (batch.close_bulk) closes settled batches in bulk: produced >= plan, nothing left, no variance
Plant Manager or COO reopens with a reason code and at least 10 characters; the close is kept in closeHistory
packing.reconcile accounts the whole remainder (loss, by-product, divert, rework, keep as stock) within 0.5

blocks.p: Reconcile does not close a batch. It can be done in parts while the batch is still producing, and a second reconcile adds to the first (26a). By-product, divert and rework go into 1 open pool per product; loss is written off with a reason; stock kept stays packable on the batch.
A reopened batch is not asked to be closed again as if nothing happened: its Close job reads 'Reopened, check first' with the reopen reason.

blocks.p: When masters.labFlow is on, a new sample goes to the QCM to assign (Assign sample), each test goes to its analyst with its own due time (Lab test), and a sample still open more than 1 day after its due time gives the Plant Manager Lab late. Only the COO switches it.

items.title: Escalation: how long a job may wait, and who is told (acEscalation)
src: docs/SPEC-04-REALTIME-DISCIPLINE.md 'A note on the escalation engine'

blocks.p: A job escalates when its waiting days (actTiming, LG-13) reach the limit. The owner keeps the job; the person it escalates to also sees it, tagged. Open Production counts from the last activity, not from the PO's age: for a bulk base, the last logged output on that base (never before the PO arrived); for a PO line, its last lot or batch opening, or raw material ready when no batch is open yet (acProduceStallDays).

list: No escalation while the line waits for the client: Pack from base, Open Production (15g).
No escalation for Open Production while the line was packed in the last 7 days (moving, 15g).
No escalation for a Pack job whose PO lines all wait for the client (15g).
Lab test: late by the clock against its own due time; days shown = whole days late (24r).

blocks.note: Stuck at packing (Supply Chain) has no escalation. Recorded as known and not built in OP-HANDOFF-O2S.md 15 Oct (11).

blocks.p: 1 rule for Plant, the Production batch list and Today. Last move = the latest shift entry or pack record on the batch (a reversed or void pack does not count). Pools, voided and by-product batches are never listed; a closed batch is judged only while it holds kept stock to pack.

blocks.p: The lines a batch serves: its own PO line, the lines of a multi-PO batch, or for a bulk base every open, acknowledged order line of that base of any age (no order-age limit since 15f).

items.title: A line moving, waiting for base, and the run for the rest (plLinePack, plLineBaseItems, plBaseShare)

list: Moving: the same product packed for the same client on any of that client's POs (any line, the same PO too) in the last 7 days. A cancelled or voided PO does not count; a PO with no client counts only itself.
A line wants base when it is acknowledged, not sent back, still owed more than 0.5, not closed, and not already served by its own ready PO or multi-PO batch.
Line clock = later of its last pack (as above), PO received and base first ready.
Pack from base: 1 card per order line while ready base > 0.5. Every line sees all the ready base; Production chooses what to pack.

Open Production for the rest: only for what the ready base and the base with the lab cannot cover across its orders, oldest PO first, lines waiting for the client last, close-short-requested lines skipped, within what raw material allows.
Stuck at packing: on day 7 of a line with nothing packed while base (or its own batch) is ready, Supply Chain gets the job (LG-16).

blocks.p: Formula detail and worked example: formulas tab F-030 and F-031.

Approve or refuse the close-short request

blocks.p: The latest mark by time decides. While waiting: the line is not stuck, nobody is told, its jobs read 0 days and are never urgent, and no Add reason job is raised. After a wait ends, the Stuck at packing job counts from the day the wait was over, and never before 15 Oct 2026 (STUCK_JOB_SINCE).

blocks.note: Marks are rows with their own id, so 2 people marking at once are both kept by the merge (audit15g 'both marks survive the merge').

list: A cover never signs both lines of 1 certificate, never approves what he reviewed, and never reviews or approves a sample he tested. Management does not sign. Only the Plant Manager names or ends a cover (labSetCover, labEndCover); the COO does not.

Self-defer (any job): the owner hides a job for 1 to 30 days (7 offered) with a reason from a fixed list (RM en route, Scheduled later, Awaiting approval, Capacity issues, Packing not available, Other). Until the date it leaves Today for everyone, including anyone it was escalated to, and the Production stuck list skips it; it is listed under Deferred (All actions, Production) and counted as on hold on Plant.
Who is on it: opening a job from Today marks it 'X is on it' for 8 hours; marks older than 1 day are dropped. It does not lock the job.

blocks.p: When Saad, Fahim, Majid, Shoaib or another holder is away, their jobs stay addressed to the role. A second holder of the same role sees them; otherwise they wait and escalate by the table in LG-12.

items.title: Shared jobs and the Your people count (jobSharers, ypJobsFor)

list: Shared: a job not addressed to 1 person, whose role (and alsoRoles) is held by 2 or more active users other than the COO, leaving out anyone the job bars (notWho). It carries a purple tag '⇄ Shared' with their names; when one does it, it closes for all.

Your people: a person's count = their role's jobs (not addressed to someone else, not barred), plus jobs escalated to their role, plus lab sign-offs they hold as a cover. Deferred jobs are left out. A shared job counts once per person and is named shared, never added twice.
Your people is shown to department leads (TD_LEADS) for their department, and to the COO for everyone.

items.title: Two people saving at once (saveNow, merge3, mergeDupNumbers)

steps.text: Edits; save waits 400 ms, then sends the whole state with X-Base-Rev
Base rev still current? yes: saved, new rev; no: 409 with the server copy
On 409: 3-way merge (base, mine, server), then save again
Gets the merged copy on the next refresh

list: The baseline after a clash is a copy of the server's own data at that rev, so my unsent change still counts as mine (26c). After a clean save the baseline is exactly what was sent (2026-07-30).
Retries: up to 5 straight away, then every 3 seconds, so a change is never left unsent.
New ids carry a random suffix per tab (nid), so 2 tabs cannot mint the same id (2026-07-28).
DC and gate pass numbers are 'highest + 1' in each copy. After a merge, a number on 2 trucks is said once and logged, and Supply Chain gets a Duplicate number job until one is changed.
Counters are not added up: a pack lost to a clash is caught by lineIssues ('lost') and goes on Needs you (07e).
Records that must survive 2 people at once carry ids: wait marks, close history, sent-back history, COA returns.

blocks.note: Audit rows written without an id can be lost when 2 people save at once (SECURITY-REGISTER S-09, raised 15 Oct 2026, about 35 writers, not fixed).

items.title: Read and sign before the app opens (16a)

steps.text: Signs in; if no sign for brief 2026-10-13-15 exists (and real orders are loaded), the read page opens first
Reads each part for his role in order; a part opens only after the one before is answered
Answers 1 question per part. Right? yes: next part; no: the part opens again, read again (8 s and its end on screen)
Types his name as on his account and ticks read and understood; 1 row added to readSigns with an id. The page closes only when the server has it
See who has signed in Back Office, Read and signed

blocks.p: Parts are chosen by role (RS_PARTS roles): for example Production reads 6, Supply Chain 7, Warehouse 5, the CFO 3, the AQCM 2, the COO all 12. Some lines and questions are only for some roles. A row keeps brief, user, name, role, typed name, time, build, parts read, wrong tries and the device. The page closes only when the last save the server confirmed carries the row; with no internet, or when a newer build is out, it says Not saved yet and keeps the answers on that device (not on a shared login). A sign made on another device closes the page within 5 seconds. 2 people signing at once are both kept (rows carry ids).

blocks.note: Build 16a is being built on 15-16 Oct 2026 and is not pushed. Never pending on seed data with no orders.

blocks.p: Shared logins (prod1, qa2 and the like, the same list Back Office calls shared): each person types their own full name, the page opens once on each phone or computer (the device id is kept in that browser), and another person on the same device opens it from the Guide. Back Office lists each person who signed on a shared login.
The page never opens on the built-in starting data (_rsSeed), for a role outside the 15, or with no orders loaded. Signed out while it is open, it closes.

items.title: A batch number packed in 2 months (16b)

steps.text: Packs a run whose bag month differs from an earlier run of the same product and batch number (any PO). It is saved at once.
May inspect the run straight away; nothing waits for the Production Manager.
Today job Packed in 2 months: opens a table of every run with its PO, Kg/L, bag month, shift and who keyed it.
Right? yes: confirm with a note of what was checked (5 characters or more); the job goes. no: fix the run under Correct a record.
A run cancelled so only 1 month is left: the job goes away by itself.

blocks.p: Counted across all POs: same product, same batch number on the bag, runs not reversed or voided and above 0 Kg/L. A run packed from 16b counts with its bag month; an older run counts with the month of its printed mfg date, but only when the number also has a 16b run (D-291). Numbers with older runs only stay in the Anomalies report. A note covers the months it names: a run cancelled later leaves it covered, a new month asks again. Only the Production Manager may confirm; Production corrects a wrong month from Batch trace (D-292). The Anomalies report shows such a number once, as Packed in 2 months, not also as the older mixed-date fault.

items.title: The inspector is the person signed in (16b)

blocks.p: On the packed lot inspection and the truck inspection the inspector is not typed: the sheet shows the name of the login, and the inspection stores it. With nobody signed in the sheet refuses. If any packing run on the sheet was keyed by the same login (byUser), or, on an old run with no byUser, by the same name, the sheet refuses: someone else inspects it. A shared QA login records its own name. Inspections saved before 16b keep the typed name. The older lot QA sheet (renderLotQA) carries the same checks but no screen opens it.

items.title: + Log a shift: the list of open batches (16b)

blocks.p: Today’s + Log a shift (people with the right shift.log) always opens a list: every batch that is open, not a pool, and can still take output (batchLogRoom above 0.5 Kg/L: up to 115% of plan, a PO batch never past its PO). Batches short of plan come first, then plan made with the room left; newest opened first within each. Log shift opens the shift form of that batch. No batch: a message says to open a batch first (D-293).

items.title: Alerts: who gets which alert, and when (16c)
src: fn pushJobsNow, pushKeyOf, pushRefOf, pushJobsFrom, pushAfterSave, pushSweep, pushStart
apps/o2s/notify-routes.js (JOB_ROLES, ESC_TO, NIGHT_ANY_HOUR, POST /api/o2s/push/jobs, deliver, releaseHeld, alertText)

blocks.p: The screen builds the job list with the same actionItems as Today (all roles), leaves out jobs put off to a later day, and gives each job a key: the Today key, or 1 per product for Open Production, 1 per PO for Receive and Add reason, 1 per test for Lab test. Each escalation is its own entry, addressed to the role it escalates to.

list: After a save the server took (Way 1): the screen compares the jobs of the copy before the save with the jobs of the copy saved, and sends only the new ones. It runs after the save is finished and never delays it. Escalations never go this way.

Every 15 minutes (Way 2): a screen that is signed in, has no save waiting, runs the current build, has the people list loaded and has the same version as the server sends its whole list. The server takes at most 1 per 10 minutes. The first list ever only records what is open, with no alerts. Later lists send what is new and close what is gone, so a job that comes back alerts again. A list closes only rows opened before it started, and closes nothing if a people lookup failed.

Who: the role the job is addressed to and its alsoRoles, only where that role is allowed for that job name; only the named person when the job names 1; never anyone the job bars. In a save, the person who saved is recorded but not alerted, so a later 15-minute list does not alert him either. Escalations only to the role in the escalation table. A person in 2 of the job's roles gets 1 alert; the any-hour role decides the night rule.

1 alert per Today card per person while it stays open: the server writes an open row per card and person, and only a new row sends (2 screens at the same moment cannot both send). More work joining an open card (Open Production by product, Receive by PO, Lab test by test) does not alert again.
Night: 10 pm to 7 am Pakistan time, office roles are held and get 1 summary at 7 am; Production, Production Manager, QA Inspector and Warehouse get alerts any hour.
A device that the push service says is gone (switched off, browser reset) is removed. An alert waits at most 6 hours for a device that is off.

Any error inside the alert addresses (a lost database connection, say) answers {ok:false}; it never stops the server or a save. Tapping an alert opens Today, unless a form has typing in it or a sheet is open: then O2S only comes to the front.

blocks.note: Jobs that come with the clock and escalations need at least 1 screen open somewhere (any person, any device) for the 15-minute check; with every screen closed, they alert at the next check after someone opens O2S.
